r.정치 구도: A constitutional monarchy with the king as head of state and a prime minister leading the government. Since absolute monarchy ended in 1932, the army has staged more than ten successful coups, the most recent in 2014. The 2017 constitution, written under military rule, gave great power to unelected bodies and the courts, so parties that win elections have repeatedly been kept from power and prime ministers removed by court rulings. In August 2025 another prime minister was removed by the Constitutional Court, over a phone call with Cambodia's leader. In the February 2026 general election a conservative party close to the palace and the army defied the polls to come first, and a referendum held the same day approved drafting a new constitution. Whether to reform the law that severely punishes criticism of the monarchy, and who will write the new constitution and how, are now the central questions.

t.why: It sits at the heart of mainland Southeast Asia, bordering Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia and Malaysia. A US ally since 1954, it hosts Cobra Gold every year, the largest multinational military exercise in Asia, yet it is also close to China through rail projects and trade. In July and December 2025 fighting broke out with Cambodia over land around ancient temples on the border, killing many people and forcing hundreds of thousands to flee. A new ceasefire was signed at the end of December, but the disputes over the land and sea boundaries remain unresolved. Myanmar's civil war also spills over into Thailand in the form of refugees and scam compounds just across the border. As a major production base for Japanese carmakers, it features prominently in stories about Southeast Asian supply chains.
t.rel: The only Southeast Asian country never colonized, it is a longtime US ally that is also close to China. It has a border dispute with Cambodia and refugee and border issues with Myanmar.
t.korea: During the Korean War it sent more than 11,000 troops in all from 1950 onward, and their bravery earned them the nickname 'Little Tigers'. Diplomatic relations were established in October 1958. Thailand is a favorite destination for Korean travelers, and Korean dramas and K-pop are hugely popular there. Thai workers also come to Korean farms and factories under Korea's Employment Permit System. At the same time, Thais make up the largest group of foreigners staying in Korea without permission, and when Korea tightened entry checks around 2024 it caused a backlash in Thailand.
t.know: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonized by a European power.
etext: Japanese carmakers began building plants in the 1960s, turning it into Southeast Asia's largest car-making base. It is especially known for pickup trucks, which it exports around the world. Recently a string of Chinese electric-vehicle makers have opened factories there too.
Tens of millions of visitors a year come to places like Bangkok, Phuket and Chiang Mai, so tourism makes up a big share of the economy. When foreign arrivals drop, growth falls right away.
It is the world's largest producer of natural rubber and a major exporter of rice, sugar, chicken and canned tuna. A large share of workers still live in the countryside.

Household debt is very high relative to income, holding back consumer spending. A low birth rate is aging the population fast, and growth tends to lag behind its neighbors. A flood of cheap Chinese goods is putting pressure on local manufacturers.
